rv.q: There’s a disarming honesty to this intriguing production, as courageous as it is charming.
It’s vividly brought to life by Fionna Hewitt-Twamley, in a virtuoso performance that has rightly won acclaim at the Edinburgh Fringe and elsewhere.
Myra’s Story is well-intentioned but its tone is constantly uneven.

cn.t: Well-intentioned solo show about homelessness features an impassioned performance but suffers from uneven tone. Critics find the familiar addiction narrative more worthy cause than compelling drama.
